text: I pick my way through the mud to the roster beside the gate and read the fresh warning about the missing patrol, looking for names, a route, or how recently it was posted.
motivation: The serjeant keeps glancing at a freshly posted warning about a patrol gone missing, and that is the clearest clue in the rain-soaked crowd.
intended: I want the exact wording of the notice so I know who vanished, where, and whether the warning is new enough to still matter.

text: I step back from the board and scan the gate approach for the crate yards, looking northwest for the mud track the notice names and whether anything there looks recently disturbed.
motivation: The warning points to a specific place, the northwest mud track behind the crate yards, and that is the only lead the posting actually gives.
intended: I want to see whether the crate yards and that track are visible from the gate, and if the ground or the crates show any sign of the missing patrol.

text: The track itself tells me nothing, so I walk into the crate yards and look between the stacks, checking the gaps and the ground behind them for anything the rain and wagon ruts would not have wiped away.
motivation: The warning named the crate yards, and the open mud only shows ordinary wagon and laborer traffic.
intended: I want to see whether something is hidden, dropped, or out of place among the crates themselves.

text: I pause between the stacks and look at the nearest guard, noting where their eyes go and whether their hand is on a weapon, then ask quietly if anyone passed through the yards since the notice went up.
motivation: The mud and straw show nothing, but the guards are watching this yard in a silence that does not match ordinary wagon traffic.
intended: I want to see whether the guards are watching the crates or watching me, and whether they saw anyone use this track.

text: I follow the guard's glance past the gate and study the road beyond, looking for whatever keeps pulling their eyes off the yards.
motivation: Their gaze leaves the empty crate yards and returns to the road, and their hand stays tight on the shortsword.
intended: I want to see what on that road is holding the guard's attention.

text: The road shows me nothing, so I turn back toward the crowd and study the threadbare figure standing apart, watching which faces they follow and whether they ever look at the gate.
motivation: That figure stands out of the line and watches people instead of the gate, while the road the guard fears is empty.
intended: I want to see who they are looking for before I decide whether to speak to them.

text: I ease closer through the crowd until I can see the same stretch of gate their eyes keep checking, and I ask, low, who they are waiting for.
motivation: Their glances keep leaving the faces and flicking to the gate, as if a person or a signal still has not arrived.
intended: I want them to name who or what they expect, and I want to be looking at the gate when it happens.

text: I let the silence stand and look into the knot of guards and refugees their eyes just left, picking out which face they lingered on and who went still when I spoke.
motivation: They would not answer, but their glance moved from the gate to that knot, and the crowd around us went quiet.
intended: I want to see which person in that group they are actually watching, and who reacted to the question.

text: I leave the stranger their silence and look across the mud at the bright townhouse, checking its door, windows, and whether anyone there is watching the gate while the crowd pretends not to.
motivation: They would not name anyone in the knot, only that someone keeps to themselves, and that house stands apart from the muddy crowd with colors the rain has not touched.
intended: I want to see if the house is closed up, occupied, or watching us, and whether it is the place people will not talk about.

text: I cross the mud to the townhouse and look past the sky in the polished windows, checking for a lamp, a face, or any movement behind the glass, and I read whatever mark or crest is on the shut door.
motivation: The door is shut and freshly painted, and no sentry stands outside, so whatever watches from that house would be inside the glass.
intended: I want to see who keeps the house, and whether anyone in it is watching the gate.
